evidenceLimits: Count probabilities assume independent draws with fixed individual modeled chances. The central range has at least 80 percent mass because counts are discrete; it is not a guarantee, confidence interval or causal test. Empirical shares can differ, and a small probability for one exact count does not by itself establish an unusual overall result.
